title: The Promise Stands
subtitle: The Hour is not a possibility. It is an appointment.
sources: Qur'an 33:63 — 'people ask you about the Hour; say: its knowledge is with Allah'
Qur'an 20:15 — 'indeed, the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives'

chapters.heading: Almost Concealed
chapters.body: The Qur'an states the end of the world the way calendars state the seasons — as settled fact: 'Indeed, the Hour is coming; I almost conceal it so that every soul may be recompensed for what it strives' (20:15). Almost concealed: close enough to shape every choice, far enough that no one builds a business on the date. The Prophet ﷺ said the Hour and his own sending were joined like these two fingers — and he asked Jibril: what is its first sign? — and the tradition records the answer's structure: ten major signs, each a catastrophe with a name (Muslim 2942). The mercy of the design is in the concealment: had the date been known, the last generation would inherit everything and earn nothing; had it been deniable, no one would prepare. So it stays almost — the appointment on the wall with no hour beneath it, and the entire art of faith is living ready for a knock that has no schedule.

familyQuestion: The date is hidden but the appointment is certain. How would you spend this week if the knock came Friday?

title: The Moon Split
subtitle: The first great sign the Qur'an itself named
sources: Qur'an 54:1-2 — 'the Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split'
Seerah: Ibn Ishaq — the Makkans' witnesses and their reaction

chapters.heading: And They Saw It
chapters.body: The Qur'an opens Surah Al-Qamar with it: 'The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And if they see a sign, they turn away and say: passing magic' (54:1-2). The seerah records the night: the Prophet ﷺ called the Quraysh in the bright moonlight and pointed, and the moon divided in two halves, one on each side of Mount Hira — and the witnesses came home swearing to what they had seen, and then did the thing the verse predicted: they called it magic and filed the miracle away. The tradition adds its gentle irony: the witnesses themselves — Walid, Abu Jahl, and others who named it sorcery — confirmed the event they denied, which is exactly how the verse framed denial: not as ignorance of the sign, but as refusal of its meaning. A miracle is not evidence for those committed to unbelief; the moon can split and the witness can shrug. Signs ask something of the heart before they ask anything of the eyes.

familyQuestion: They saw the moon split and called it magic. What have you seen with your own eyes that you're explaining away?

title: The Minor Signs
subtitle: The syllabus of the centuries — read as milestones, not dates
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 47 — 'time will pass rapidly... the barefoot naked will compete in building tall structures'
Sahih Muslim 2947 — knowledge lifted, ignorance paraded
Qur'an 81:1-14 — the surah of the falling signs

chapters.heading: Knowledge Lifted
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ mapped the centuries in single sentences, and the hadith collections preserve the map: time will compress until a year passes like a month, a month like a week (Bukhari 1036); knowledge will be lifted and ignorance will rule — meaning the knowledgeable dying and the ignorant leading (Bukhari 98); drinking and music will spread until generations are raised on them; the barefoot and naked will compete in the height of buildings (Bukhari 47); a man will obey his wife and disobey his mother, and treat his friend and abandon his father (Tirmidhi 2210). Each generation has read the list and seen its own decade in it — which is precisely the design: the signs are not a countdown but a curriculum, issued so that every century would find its warnings addressed to it personally. The minor signs end where Surah At-Takwir ends: 'so where are you going? It is only a reminder to the worlds' (81:26-27). The signs are not there to date the Hour. They are there to wake the sleeper.

familyQuestion: Every generation found its own decade in the list. Which lines describe your decade most exactly?

title: The Ten Major Signs
subtitle: The appointed sequence — every chain in the hadith agrees on the order
sources: Sahih Muslim 2942 — the ten, in order: Dajjal, descent of Isa, Ya'juj-Ma'juj, three sinkings, smoke, the Beast, sunrise from the west, fire
Muslim 2947 — like beads falling one after another

chapters.heading: One After Another
chapters.body: The hadith of al-Hudhayfa names them in sequence, and the collections agree on the order: the Dajjal; the descent of Isa son of Maryam; the release of Ya'juj and Ma'juj; three great sinkings of the earth — east, west, and Arabia; the Smoke; the Beast; the sunrise from the west; and finally the Fire that drives mankind to their gathering (Muslim 2942). The Prophet ﷺ said they will come 'like beads falling from a string — the first and the last without a gap' (Muslim 2947). Notice the mercy in the sequence: each sign is bigger than the one before, and the biggest are saved for the end — no one will be able to say they were not warned in order. And notice the comfort buried in the list: after the Dajjal comes Isa, and after the sinkings and smoke comes the Fire — and the Fire is the last one, because it gathers the people for judgment itself. The sequence ends at the Throne. Every road in the ten signs points to one address.

familyQuestion: The signs come in order, each bigger than the last. If the syllabus is ordered, what should you learn first?

title: The Smoke
subtitle: Forty days that cover the believer and touch the disbeliever
sources: Qur'an 44:10-11 — 'so watch for the day when the sky brings a visible smoke, covering the people; this is a painful punishment'
Sahih al-Bukhari 3231 — its effect: believers like a cold's touch, disbelievers smothered

chapters.heading: A Filter in the Sky
chapters.body: 'So watch for the day when the sky brings a visible smoke, covering the people — this is a painful punishment' (44:10-11). The hadith describes its physics and its justice: the smoke covers the sky for forty days, descending until it covers the people — and for the believer it touches like a cold, like a sniffle passing — nothing more — 'but for the disbeliever it is like being smothered, coming from every opening of his body' (Bukhari 3231). One sky, two weathers: the same covering that is barely a nuisance to faith is a suffocation to rejection. The smoke is a preview of the judgment itself, where the identical event — standing before the same Lord — is mercy for one soul and anguish for another, and the difference was never the event. The Hour's signs don't create the two kinds of people. They simply stop letting them hide from the difference.

familyQuestion: The same smoke is a sniffle for one and smothering for the other. What 'same event' are you and someone else experiencing in opposite weathers right now?

title: The Beast
subtitle: A speaker from the earth marking every soul
sources: Qur'an 27:82 — 'and when the word falls upon them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them'
Sahih Muslim 2942 — the Beast among the ten signs

chapters.heading: The Earth's Witness
chapters.body: 'And when the word falls upon them — because they did not believe in Our signs — We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, that the people were not certain of Our signs' (27:82). The hadith gives the encounter its detail: the Prophet ﷺ described the Beast as marked — three letters written between its eyes, readable by the literate and the illiterate alike — and said it will emerge and strike the forehead of every person, and by that mark the believer and disbeliever are sorted (Abu Dawud, al-Malaahim; Tirmidhi 3143, hasan). The Qur'an's own phrasing is the lesson: the Beast 'speaks to them' — the earth itself becomes a witness when the people would not hear the prophets. And the timing in the sequence matters: the Beast comes late, when the arguments have all been made and the denials have all hardened. Some hearts only understand when the ground they stood on rises and speaks.

familyQuestion: The earth itself will testify. What is the ground of your life saying about you right now — before it has to speak?

title: The Sun Rises from the West
subtitle: The door that closes with the light
sources: Qur'an 6:158 — 'the day some of your Lord's signs come, no soul will benefit from its faith'
Sahih Muslim 2942 — the sunrise from the west as a major sign
Sahih al-Bukhari 4636 — no repentance accepted after it

chapters.heading: When Seeing Stops Counting
chapters.body: The order of nature is the last argument: 'The day some of your Lord's signs come, no soul will benefit from its faith — a faith it had not before — nor from any recompense earned' (6:158). The hadith names the sign: the sun rises from the west — the direction of the whole creation reversed in a single morning — and with that reversal, the door of repentance is closed until the Judgment (Bukhari 4636). The scholars draw the circle precisely: every sign before this one is a summons, and this one is the deadline — after it, seeing is believing and believing no longer avails, because the trial was built for the unseen. 'It is He who made the night and day an alternation for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude' (25:62) — the alternation itself was the proof, repeated every twenty-four hours, free of charge, for a lifetime. The sunrise will simply be the morning the proof stops being subtle.

familyQuestion: The sun rises from the west only when it's too late. What are you treating as 'too subtle' that is actually your daily proof?

title: The Week of the Dajjal
subtitle: Seven days that test every soul alive
sources: Sahih Muslim 2942-2943 — the Dajjal's itinerary: forty days, one like a year, one like a month, one like a week, the rest like your days
Sahih al-Bukhari 7135 — 'there was no prophet but he warned his people'

chapters.heading: Forty Days of Fire and Rain
chapters.body: The hadith draws the week in detail: the Dajjal stays forty days — one day like a year, one like a month, one like a week, and the rest like your days — and he travels every highway except Makkah and Madinah, which the angels turn him from; with him is a garden and a fire, and his fire is coolness and his garden is flame (Muslim 2942). His temptations are not crude: he brings provision to those who follow him and famine to those who refuse — the economics of obedience inverted, as if the whole test of life were run in forty accelerated days. And the Prophet ﷺ said: since the creation of Adam there has been no fitnah like the fitnah of the Dajjal (Muslim 2946) — the concentration of every trial humanity has ever known, compressed into one figure, for one week. The exit was given before the trial was: al-Kahf's first and last verses, memorized before his arrival, and the Prophet ﷺ said: he will not harm whoever recites them (Muslim 2940). The greatest test in history came with its answer key, published fourteen centuries early.

familyQuestion: The greatest trial came with its answer key. Do you know the first and last verses of al-Kahf by heart yet?

title: The Descent of Isa
subtitle: The return the prophets promised and the Qur'an sealed
sources: Qur'an 4:157-159 — 'and there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in him before his death'
Sahih al-Bukhari 2476 — the descent, the cross broken, the Qur'an ruling
Sahih Muslim 2940 — Isa kills the Dajjal at the gate of Ludd

chapters.heading: He Descends at the White Minaret
chapters.body: The hadith fixes the scene: Isa son of Maryam descends at the white minaret in the eastern part of the Damascus mosque, his hands resting on the wings of two angels (Bukhari 2476). He comes not to begin a new revelation but to complete this one: he breaks the cross, kills the swine, abolishes the jizyah — no one left to pay it, all either believing or perishing — and rules by this Qur'an as a Muslim among Muslims, praying behind the Mahdi as one of the ummah (Bukhari 2476). His first act of judgment is the Dajjal's end: at the gate of Ludd in Palestine, Isa catches him, and the narration says the Dajjal melts like salt in water at the sight of him — or dissolves by Isa's spear (Muslim 2940). The Qur'an sealed the theology in advance: 'and there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death, and on the Day of Resurrection he will be a witness against them' (4:159). The world's longest argument ends with the living Witness standing among them.

familyQuestion: Isa returns to rule by the Qur'an. What does it mean that every road in history ends at the same Book?

title: Ya'juj and Ma'juj Released
subtitle: The wall stands by decree; the release is scheduled
sources: Qur'an 18:98 — 'when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level'
Qur'an 21:96-97 — 'from every elevated place they descend, and the true promise draws near'

chapters.heading: Level Ground
chapters.body: 'Until when Gog and Magog are opened, and from every elevated place they descend, and the true promise draws near, and suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring' (21:96-97). The hadith fills the release with sound: every day the hordes tunnel at the wall, and every evening their leader says: come back tomorrow — and each day the tunnel is restored, until the day he says — in Allah's name, we will finish it tomorrow — and returns to find the wall like it was (Muslim 2949). The sentence history repeats in al-Kahf's daily recitation — 'the promise of my Lord is ever true' (18:98) — becomes the event. Their surge, the tradition says, drains Lake Tiberias; Isa and the believers withdraw to Mount Tur; and the ending is sudden and strange: Allah sends a worm in their necks, and by morning they are all dead — a nation that terrified the world dies in one night by the smallest of creatures (Bukhari 3348). The loudest trial in the sequence ends in silence.

familyQuestion: A nation that terrified the world died in one night by a worm. What giant in your life is smaller than it looks?

title: The Breeze and the Fire
subtitle: The angel in the east gathers what remains
sources: Sahih Muslim 2942 — the fire as the tenth sign
Qur'an 50:42 — 'the day they hear the blast in truth'
Qur'an 39:68-69 — the two blasts and the earth shining with its Lord's light

chapters.heading: A Wind from the East
chapters.body: After the sinkings, after the smoke, after the Beast and the reversed sun and the returned Isa and the dead hordes — the last sign is the gathering: a fire from Yemen, or a wind, the traditions name both routes, driving the people to Sham, to the plain of gathering (Muslim 2942). The hadith says an angel is sent to the east, and the first of the creation he breathes upon — every soul still alive — tastes death at his breath (Muslim 2879's companion tradition). Then the silence: 'And the Trumpet will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead, except whom Allah wills' (39:68). And after the silence, the second blast: 'and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten' (36:51). The fire that gathers them is the last sign because it delivers them to the appointment itself — the plain where, the Qur'an says, 'the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the record will be placed, the prophets and the witnesses brought, and it will be judged between them in truth' (39:69).

familyQuestion: The gathering is the last sign because it's the first moment of the meeting. Ready or not — what's your status?

title: The End of the Story
subtitle: The kingdom that never ends
sources: Qur'an 39:69-70 — 'and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged'
Qur'an 21:104 — 'the Day We will fold the heaven like the folding of a written sheet for the records'
Qur'an 98:8 — 'their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence'

chapters.heading: Folding the Sky
chapters.body: The Qur'an ends the world the way a scribe ends a scroll: 'The Day We will fold the heaven like the folding of a written sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it — a promise upon Us; indeed, We will do it' (21:104). Then the judgment: 'the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, the record will be laid out, the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged' (39:69). And then the story that outlasts the sky itself opens: 'Their reward with their Lord is gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever — Allah being pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord' (98:8). The Last Day is not the end of the story; it is the end of the chapter titled *Trial*. The book it opens has no final page — 'a promise binding upon Us; indeed, We will do it' (21:104). Every sign in this shelf exists to make that page reachable.

familyQuestion: The world ends like a folded scroll — and the next book has no last page. Which book are you writing your page for right now?
